summary: With timed wounded legs, the recorded #ride answer declines the optional debug force prompt. C intentionally refuses the mount after printing “Your leg is in no shape for riding.” JavaScript currently throws UnsupportedSteedError at this guard, stopping before the expected screen and cursor. This is a missing branch in the partially ported steed.c:mount_steed function; the shared wounded-leg feedback and healing helpers already exist in js/do.js.

source.branch: When Wounded_legs is true at mount_steed entry, the function calls legs_in_no_shape("riding", FALSE). It then asks “Heal your legs?” only when force && wizard; otherwise, including the recorded declined force prompt, it returns FALSE without mounting. An accepted force-heal answer clears the wound and continues through the remaining mount checks.
callers: steed.c:doride() (177-192), which obtains the force answer and returns mount_steed() as ECMD_TIME or ECMD_OK
cmd.c:extcmdlist doride entry (around 1834), which exposes the production #ride command
dependencies: do.c:heal_legs() (2448-2486), already implemented in js/do.js and used by the force && wizard affirmative branch
youprop.h:Wounded_legs/HWounded_legs/EWounded_legs; JavaScript stores the timeout and wounded-side bits in WOUNDED_LEGS intrinsic/extrinsic state

evidence: challenges/manifests/v26.json records the case route: steed.c:doride asks the debug force question; the response at step 27 is n; C emits “Your leg is in no shape for riding.” at step 28.

nethack-c/upstream/src/steed.c:178-192 shows doride passing the force flag to mount_steed and mapping FALSE to ECMD_OK. nethack-c/upstream/src/steed.c:225-238 shows the wounded-leg guard, feedback call, optional force-heal question, and intentional FALSE return.

nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:2408-2423 defines legs_in_no_shape, which derives side and singular/plural wording from EWounded_legs. js/do.js:3053-3077 already implements this feedback helper; js/do.js:3128-3159 implements heal_legs for the force affirmative branch.

js/steed.js:456-482 currently throws UnsupportedSteedError when WOUNDED_LEGS is active instead of calling legs_in_no_shape and following C’s conditional heal-or-return path. The saved evaluation reports the first mismatch at step 28 with matched RNG (2733/2733), and missing screen/cursor output from the JavaScript stop.

Selection scope is the whole steed.c:mount_steed function, as required for a C file-port. Its existing doride caller is already wired in js/steed.js; the implementation task must retain that production path and remove the unsupported placeholder when the complete function is ported.
